title: Tool holders reference a library entry: collision, simulation and preview read one resolved holder shape

labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Part of #2007.

Maintainer in chat, 2026-11-15: "That tool editor issue is a P3".

## What happens

- A tool keeps its own holder as `holder_d`/`holder_len` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:203-204`).
- A library holder is copied, not referenced. `SetToolBody::library` (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_body.rs:155-169`) writes the library outline into the tool as a drawn spun body. The tool keeps no link to the library entry.
- The holder fit is thus sized for each tool by hand.

## What to do

1. Add a tool key `holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` that names a library entry (`holder_library::find`, `crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs:345`).
2. Resolve the reference to a `HolderProfile` in the one seam: `tool_body::judged`, `stack` and `digest` (`crates/app/src/tool_body.rs:173-224`). Each collision law and the simulation (`sim_tool_body.rs:196-197`) then read the same shape.
3. Keep the #828 floor for a machine-default holder.
4. Migration: an old drawn library copy and an old `holder_d`/`holder_len` cylinder load as a custom holder with the same shape. Use the version step of the cutting-data sub-issue (`PROJECT_VERSION` 62, `.camtools` 2), or take the next one if that sub-issue is not merged.
5. A reference to an entry that does not exist refuses the file by name. It never falls back to a different holder (see #808).
6. Fill the holder fields from the entry. The user does not size them.

This changes the shape that collision checks and simulation read: `effort:max` by the safety floor.

## Done means:

- A tool with a library holder stores the reference, not a copy.
- `judged` and `stack` give the same bands for a referenced holder and for its old copy. A test pins this.
- An old project and an old `.camtools` file load with no change to any collision result. A test pins this.
- An unknown entry name refuses the file by name.
- The `set_tool_holder` MCP tool (#799) writes the reference.
- The PR is `feat!` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

Order: after the layout sub-issue. The Weldon sub-issue needs this one.
